verdict: NOT REFUTED. I wrote a separate engine from data/us.csv and data/kr.csv without reading the replication code, and it supports the claim: the reported performance needs the KR night leg to be sized with brake/cooldown state and equity that only exist after the US session lying inside that night. My engine reproduces the package's own US-only "v8" yearly table for 2000-2025 with RMSE 0.10 pp (max 0.3 pp, MDD -68.0% vs reported -68.0%), so the US legs, costs, tax and overlay conventions are pinned and the only open degree of freedom is the KR leg. With the plan.py loop (T2), v10 gives 61.0 / 65.2 / 57.1% for 2010-03.. / 2013.. / 2015.. (to 2026-10-07) and PRESET_A 78.4 / 76.7 / 67.8%. With entry-time state and equity (T1), v10 gives 36.2 / 44.3 / 35.7% and PRESET_A 18.1 / 26.1 / 17.2%, so the gap is 21-25 pp for v10 and 51-60 pp for PRESET_A. No innocent modelling choice closes it: the best of 144 stacked combinations of KR proxy, cash interest, cooldown counting, tax/peak rule, crisis-flag timing and within-row compounding (the cost formula was checked separately, +0.1 / +0.6 pp), with stated costs and tax kept, lifts T1 to 44.6% for v10 (report-implied 64.1%) and 20.9% for PRESET_A (T2 76.7%). Two falsification tests confirm the mechanism: shuffling the KR nights makes T2 equal T1 (mean gap +0.2 / 0.0 pp), and a zero-premium placebo KR leg still adds +4.7 pp over US-only for PRESET_A under T2 while costing -37 pp under T1. Two caveats: my T2 does not reproduce the KR-inclusive report figures exactly (v10 within 0.1-7 pp, v11-A 2-10 pp short, v9 yearly RMSE 5-8 pp), so "the package used T2" remains a strong inference rather than a reading of g2.py/uni.py; and for v10 on 2013.. and 2015.. the KR leg under T1 is about neutral on CAGR in my engine, not clearly negative as the replication lane states.

findings.title: The T1/T2 gap is real and large in an independently written engine
findings.detail: Applying b from the start of the exit row and running equity to the KR night (plan.py lines 52, 59-63) versus state and equity at the KR close of entry changes v10 from 36.2 / 44.3 / 35.7% to 61.0 / 65.2 / 57.1% (2010-03.. / 2013.. / 2015.., to 2026-10-07) and PRESET_A from 18.1 / 26.1 / 17.2% to 78.4 / 76.7 / 67.8%. A separate event-driven replay of the live scheduler gives v10 34.2% and PRESET_A 11.9% for 2010-03... Three tradable implementations (entry-state row engine, entry-row additive booking, event replay) agree within a few pp of each other and sit 20-60 pp below the package loop.

findings.title: Only the package-loop convention comes near the report numbers
findings.detail: With US legs validated to 0.1 pp RMSE against the report's v8 yearly table, the KR convention is the only free choice. v10 to end-2025: T2 62.0-64.0 / 66.6-69.2 / 58.2-61.1 / 75.4-81.0 against report-implied 64.1 / 68.2 / 61.7 / 82.4, and the same loss-year list (2011, 2015, 2018, 2022). T1 gives 36.3 / 43.6 / 35.7 / 52.5 and entry-row booking 47.1 / 52.7 / 45.0 / 65.3; both add 2016 as a loss year. v11-A: T2 81.5-83.8 / 67.7-70.2 / 79.9-84.1 against 85.9 / 74.5 / 84.5; T1 24.3 / 12.2 / 9.2. v9 yearly table: T2 RMSE 6-8 pp, T1 22-24 pp, entry-row booking 18.5-19.5 pp.
findings.evidence: out_run3.txt, out_run8.txt (US anchor), out_run5.txt, out_run4.txt, out_run9.txt

findings.title: No innocent modelling difference explains the reported numbers under tradable timing
findings.detail: Single effects on T1 CAGR (2010-03..2025) are small: cost formula +0.1 / +0.6 pp, cash interest up to +1.9 / +1.1, KR proxy between -5.4 and +3.1 / -3.6 and +0.9, cooldown counted per US close -0.9 / -4.5, tax lowering the peak +0.2 / 0.0, additive within-row compounding -0.4 / -2.7 (v10 / PRESET_A). The best of 144 stacked combinations, with stated costs and tax kept, is 44.6% for v10 and 20.9% for PRESET_A. Only removing all costs and all tax on top brings v10 to 66.6%; PRESET_A still reaches only 34.2%. Across 48 innocent settings the best T1 fit to the v9 yearly table is RMSE 15.4 pp against 5.3 pp for T2.

findings.title: Mechanism confirmed directly: the back-test cuts KR nights already known to be bad
findings.detail: The cooldown is triggered by the US session inside the KR night (correlation 0.52 with the KR night; -0.06 for the last US close before entry). The nights that only the package loop shrinks average -1.23% (v10, 99 nights, 93% negative) and -0.92% (PRESET_A, 232 nights, 88% negative). The first nights a trader could cut average +0.06% / +0.12%. Shuffling the KR nights removes the gap (T2-T1 = +0.2 / 0.0 pp over 30 shuffles). A zero-premium placebo KR leg with real costs still beats US-only by 4.7 pp for PRESET_A under T2 while losing 37 pp under T1.

findings.title: The P&L-base effect is independent of the overlay and survives additive booking
findings.detail: With brake and cooldown switched off, using the exit row's equity as the KR base gives v10 56.5% against 47.8% at entry equity (US-only 45.5%), and PRESET_A 69.1% against 47.9% (US-only 51.5%). Using row-start equity for every leg (T2-additive) leaves T2 almost unchanged (v10 62.5 vs 62.0%), because the exit row's starting equity already contains the US session inside the night. Entry-row booking with sequential compounding gains about 7 pp over its additive form from the same cross term (v10 47.1 vs 39.6%).
findings.evidence: out_run2.txt section B (last three lines per strategy), out_run5.txt

findings.title: My T2 does not reproduce the KR-inclusive report figures exactly
findings.detail: v10 windows are within 0.1-3.5 pp (up to 7 pp for 2020~ depending on the crisis-flag variant). v11-A is 2-7 pp short on windows and 10 pp short on the 2010s decade (84.8% vs 94.6%); its equity multiple from end-2011 to end-2016 is 15.6x against the plan document's 20.9x. The v9 yearly table has RMSE 5-8 pp, with 2023 the largest miss (+52 to +58% vs +71%). So "the package engines used T2" is a strong inference from fit plus plan.py, not a direct reading; g2.py and uni.py were not uploaded. Every tradable convention is 15-70 pp further away.

findings.title: Nuance against the replication verdict: under T1 the v10 KR leg is about neutral on 2013.. and 2015..
findings.detail: The replication lane says the KR leg lowers v10 CAGR versus US-only on 2010-03.., 2013.. and 2015... In my engine it is clearly lower only on 2010-03.. (36.2% vs 41.4%). On 2013.. it is 44.3% vs 43.7% and on 2015.. 35.7% vs 35.4%; the live replay gives 41.9% vs 42.1% and 34.7% vs 33.9%. MDD is about 8 pp deeper in all cases. For PRESET_A the KR leg is negative on every window (18.1 vs 35.5, 26.1 vs 32.9, 17.2 vs 27.1).

findings.title: KR crisis-flag timing stays undecided
findings.detail: Taking the KR crisis flag from the US close inside the night fits the v10 windows better (mean absolute gap 0.8 pp vs 3.6 pp), but the entry-time flag fits the reported 2022 return better (-39% vs -34%, report -40%). Size inside T2 to end-2025: +2.0 pp (v10) and +6.5 pp (PRESET_A) on 2010-03..; inside T1 +2.0 / +0.5 pp.

findings.title: KR proxy construction is not an explanation
findings.detail: (lev_n - inv_n)/3 captures 74% of the spot ETF night return over 2010-03..2026-10, the same share the v10 report states for its futures series (54% vs 51% for 2010-17, 85% vs 89% for 2018-26). Alternative proxies move T1 by -5.4 to +3.1 pp for v10. Multiplying every KR night return by 1.5 to 3 does not raise T1 above 38.4% for v10 and lowers PRESET_A.

open_issues: g2.py / uni.py were not uploaded, so the row alignment of kon[r] and the b applied to it in the report engines is inferred from plan.py plus numerical fit; my T2 fit is close but not exact (v10 0.1-7 pp, v11-A 2-10 pp, v9 yearly RMSE 5-8 pp).
Pre-2010 KR claims (1999-2026 48.9% / 77.6%, 1986 and 1929 figures) could not be tested: no KR futures proxy before 2010-02-23 and the synthetic series was not uploaded.
Data ends 2026-10-07; the reports run to 2026-11-06. My YTD against the reports' YTD implies about -41% (v10) to -48% (v8) in that month, which I could not simulate.

PRESET_A without bond has no published window figures; it was checked only through v11-A (bond 2x, whether b scales the bond is unknown) and the plan-doc table, where my T2 gives 15.6x against 20.9x for end-2011 to end-2016.

T1 for PRESET_A is sensitive to cooldown bookkeeping: 18.1% in the row engine, 12.8% with cooldown counted per US close, 11.9% in the event replay (2010-03..). The direction and size of the gap to T2 are unaffected.
The event replay marks equity at the KR close without unrealised US-night P&L (daily data only) and ignores contract rounding and margin caps.
The v9 spot-proxy fit uses BOK base rates typed from memory for the KR carry; this affects only the v9 yearly fit, not the v10 / PRESET_A results.
KR crisis-flag timing in the package (entry-time vs US close inside the night) is undecided: windows favour the latter, the 2022 return favours the former.
